tasks.title: Modify manifest.ts
tasks.description:
MODIFY src/plugins/manifest.ts. Add optional `architectures` and `principles` and `projectScope` selectors plus `"define"` scope. Tests: src/plugins/manifest.test.ts

Resolved review finding (code): Manifest parser accepts incomplete framework selectors — FR-002 and ADR-012.
  WHERE: src/plugins/manifest.ts:122-159,285-292
  EXPECTED: SkillManifestSchema.safeParse and AnyManifestSchema.safeParse reject an enforcement manifest with framework: "Svelte" and an omitted or blank language. A declared framework must be nonblank. Manifests that omit both selectors still parse with scope: "all".
  ACTUAL: Both parsers return success: true for framework: "Svelte" with no language. AnyManifestSchema also accepts framework: "". An isolated install of the Svelte fixture reached the current implementation enforcement prompt.
  FIX: Validate the framework and language pair in the enforcement manifest parse path shared by both schemas. Add phase-gated parser tests for an absent language, blank selectors, a valid pair and an unscoped legacy manifest.

Resolved review finding (T007, gate: gates/phase-02.sh, re-opened by review):
The review agent raised a finding on this task and its gate still passes, so the gate does not cover what review found. Add a test that fails on it, then fix, before completing.

DIAGNOSIS (iteration 2):
FIX: src/plugins/manifest.ts — Set both enforcement selectors to `z.string().trim().min(1).optional()`. Refine `SkillManifestSchema` after `z.discriminatedUnion("tier", ...)` to require `language` when an enforcement skill declares `framework`. Set the issue path to `["language"]` and keep `SkillManifestSchema` as the skill branch of `AnyManifestSchema`. In `src/plugins/manifest.test.ts`, exercise both `safeParse` methods with Svelte and an omitted, empty, or whitespace-only language, and with TypeScript and an empty or whitespace-only framework. Assert that TypeScript with Svelte parses and that omitting both selectors defaults `scope` to `"all"`.
FIX: src/domain/policy-selection.ts — In `src/domain/architecture-context.ts`, store bundled entries as `{ guidance: string; languages: readonly string[] }` and export `lookupFrameworkBinding` using the existing normalized key and `Object.hasOwn` guard. Assign Python to FastAPI and Django, TypeScript and JavaScript to Fastify, Express, React, and Next.js, Go to Gin and Chi, and Rust to Axum and Clap. Keep `lookupFrameworkGuidance` returning the binding’s text and use it for the existing `contextMarkdown` lookup. Import `lookupFrameworkBinding` from `./architecture-context.js` and compare its languages with `profileLanguages(input.profile)` in `composeEffectivePolicy`. Return bundled text only on a language match. With no compatible framework skill, classify a known bundle with a language mismatch as `incompatible-framework-policy` and preserve the existing missing-binding fallback. In `src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts`, assert that Django with TypeScript and `candidates: []` returns undefined guidance and an incompatible gap for Django. Assert that Django with Python returns ORM guidance and `gaps: []`.
FIX: src/domain/policy-selection.ts — Share the workflow and project identity checks between `evaluateEnforcementCandidate` and `resolveCandidates`. In `resolveCandidates`, keep the layer precedence check first, then reject scope and project identity mismatches, then let an eligible `disabled: true` copy set `suppressedByDisabled` before evaluating language, framework, architecture, or principles. Record lower same-name copies as `shadowed-by-override`. In `src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts`, compose a Clean TypeScript/Svelte profile with a global policy and a same-name project-local implementation override declaring `disabled: true` and `architectures: ["layered"]`. Assert that implementation selects neither copy and records the global copy as shadowed. Assert that review still selects the global copy and that a `projectScope: "gwrk"` disable leaves the global copy selected on an external project.
FIX: specs/044-architecture-aware-policy/gates/phase-02.sh — Keep the existing `manifest.test.ts` and `policy-selection.test.ts` entries. Add the regressions first and run the gate to observe all three defects fail. Apply the fixes and rerun the gate to verify GREEN.

Resolved review finding (code): Legacy manifests with an empty language lose their workflow scope — TR-003, FR-002.
  WHERE: src/plugins/manifest.ts:122-129,154-170
  EXPECTED: A legacy enforcement manifest with scope: "review", language: "", and no framework parses through both manifest schemas. It keeps review scope and has no language restriction.
  ACTUAL: Both schemas return a too_small issue at ["language"]. Before phase-02 both schemas parsed the fixture with scope: "review". The prior runtime treated the empty language as absent.
  FIX: Accept an empty legacy language as absent when the manifest omits framework. Keep the nonblank language requirement for framework policies. Add a phase-gated regression through both schemas for the legacy review manifest and keep the invalid framework-pair cases.

Resolved review finding (T007, gate: gates/phase-02.sh, Resolved review finding block appended, status left unchanged):
The review agent raised a finding on this task and its gate still passes, so the gate does not cover what review found. Add a test that fails on it, then fix, before completing.
Resolution: 5f92e03d passes 89 phase checks after eight observed regression failures. Native gwrk tasks done runs reverified T007, T008 and T009. Legacy review scope, returned-value isolation and framework placeholders are covered. Independent review remains pending.

Resolved review finding (code): Empty framework rejects a legacy review manifest — TR-003.
  WHERE: src/plugins/manifest.ts:125-129,154-170
  EXPECTED: A TypeScript enforcement manifest with scope: "review" and framework: "" parses through both public schemas. It keeps review scope and applies without a framework selector.
  ACTUAL: z.string().trim().min(1).optional() rejects framework: "" in both schemas. Both pre-phase schemas accepted it, and the previous runtime skipped framework filtering for an empty string.
  FIX: Normalize the legacy empty string to an absent framework before validating the selector. Keep rejecting a real framework with no language. Add a phase-gated regression through both schemas.

Resolved review finding (T007, gate: gates/phase-02.sh, re-opened by review):
The review agent raised a finding on this task and its gate still passes, so the gate does not cover what review found. Add a test that fails on it, then fix, before completing.

FIX: src/plugins/manifest.ts — Wrap `EnforcementSkillManifestSchema.framework` in `z.preprocess` to map exact `""` to `undefined` before `z.string().trim().min(1).optional()`. Keep the `SkillManifestSchema` refinement that requires a nonblank language for a real framework.
FIX: src/plugins/manifest.test.ts — Replace the empty-framework rejection case with a TypeScript `scope: "review"` regression through `SkillManifestSchema` and `AnyManifestSchema`. Assert both preserve review scope and produce `framework: undefined`. Verify the parsed skill applies in review to a TypeScript profile without a framework. Keep the whitespace-only framework and missing-language rejection cases.
FIX: src/domain/architecture-context.ts — In `normalizeFramework`, replace punctuation stripping with `value === "next.js" ? "nextjs" : value`. Keep trimming, lowercasing, and placeholder handling. Use the shared normalization for bundled lookup, candidate matching, and coverage.
FIX: src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts — Assert `lookupFrameworkGuidance("React+")` returns `undefined`. Assert a TypeScript `Framework#` profile excludes a `Framework+` policy with `framework-mismatch` and reports `missing-framework-binding` for `Framework#`. Verify a `nextjs` policy matches a padded `Next.js` profile and that composition returns bundled guidance.
FIX: src/domain/policy-selection.ts — Add `"disabled"` to `CandidateEvaluation["reason"]` and mirror it in `specs/044-architecture-aware-policy/contracts/policy-selection.md`. Return `{ included: false, reason: "disabled" }` from `evaluateEligibleCandidate` before selector checks. In `resolveCandidates`, call `evaluateEnforcementCandidate` after the precedence check. Use its `"disabled"` result to record the exclusion and mark lower same-name copies `shadowed-by-override`. Keep workflow and project identity checks ahead of disable handling.
FIX: src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts — Assert `evaluateEnforcementCandidate` returns `{ included: false, reason: "disabled" }` for a matching project-local TypeScript and Svelte review candidate. Assert `composeEffectivePolicy` selects neither copy and reports the same-name global copy as `shadowed-by-override`. Run `specs/044-architecture-aware-policy/gates/phase-02.sh` with all three regressions before and after the fixes to verify RED and GREEN.

Resolved review finding (code): Whitespace-only framework drops a legacy review skill — TR-003.
  WHERE: src/plugins/manifest.ts:129-132; src/plugins/manifest.test.ts:128-132,156-178
  EXPECTED: Both manifest schemas parse an existing enforcement skill with scope: "review", language: "TypeScript", and framework: "   ". The skill has no framework restriction and its content loads only in review.
  ACTUAL: Both schemas reject framework: "   " with too_small at framework, so the loader omits the skill. The pre-phase schemas accepted it. The current phase gate asserts rejection while its compatibility case covers framework: "" only.
  FIX: Normalize a string whose trim() is empty to undefined before validating the framework selector. Keep the language requirement for a nonblank framework. Cover both empty strings and whitespace-only strings in the legacy review test through both schemas.

Resolved review finding (T007, gate: gates/phase-02.sh, Resolved review finding block appended, status left unchanged):
The review agent raised a finding on this task and its gate still passes, so the gate does not cover what review found. Add a test that fails on it, then fix, before completing.
Resolution: Blank framework compatibility failed four regression cases before normalization. All 95 phase checks pass after the repair. Prior punctuation and disabled-candidate repairs remain covered. Independent review remains pending.

tasks.title: Create policy-selection.ts
tasks.description:
NEW src/domain/policy-selection.ts. Implement pure `evaluateEnforcementCandidate` and `composeEffectivePolicy` with override precedence and gap records. Tests: src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts

Resolved review finding (code): Framework gap contradicts bundled guidance — FR-002.
  WHERE: src/domain/policy-selection.ts:284-318
  EXPECTED: composeEffectivePolicy({ profile: { type: "webapp", stack: { language: "TypeScript", framework: "Fastify" }, design }, candidates: [] }) returns frameworkGuidance defined and gaps without "missing-framework-binding". Record "missing-framework-binding" only when lookupFrameworkGuidance(framework) is undefined and no framework candidate exists. This matches the language gap rule at lines 271-282.
  ACTUAL: The same result carries frameworkGuidance (the bundled Fastify text) and gaps: [{ kind: "missing-framework-binding", subject: "Fastify", message: "No bundled framework binding or policy for Fastify." }]. Django, FastAPI, Express, React, Next.js, Gin, Chi, Axum and Clap behave the same. Phase 4 contextMarkdown would render a false gap beside the bundled guidance and change manifest hashes for every project without an installed pack.
  FIX: In the framework gap block, push "missing-framework-binding" only when !hasSelectedFrameworkSkill && !hadFrameworkCandidate && lookupFrameworkGuidance(framework) === undefined. Keep "incompatible-framework-policy" when framework candidates exist and none is compatible. Add a src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts case for Fastify with candidates: [] asserting frameworkGuidance is defined and gaps toEqual([]). Keep the Svelte case asserting "missing-framework-binding". Run gates/phase-02.sh before the fix to observe RED.

Resolved review finding (T009, gate: gates/phase-02.sh, Resolved review finding block appended, status left unchanged):
The review agent raised a finding on this task and its gate still passes, so the gate does not cover what review found. Add a test that fails on it, then fix, before completing.

Resolved review finding (code): Framework gap misclassifies disabled, out-of-scope and gwrk-scoped candidates — FR-002 and FR-005.
  WHERE: src/domain/policy-selection.ts:285-318
  EXPECTED: A disabled Fastify override returns no framework gap. A compatible Fastify skill with scope "implementation" also returns no gap under scope "define". On an external project, a projectScope "gwrk" skill returns no gap for Fastify and returns "missing-framework-binding" for Svelte. A Fastify skill with scope "implementation" and architectures ["layered"] still returns "incompatible-framework-policy" under scope "define".
  ACTUAL: hadFrameworkCandidate matches every candidate naming Fastify. disabledResult in src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts lines 139-153 emits "incompatible-framework-policy". Scope "define" over an implementation-only skill and external projects with a gwrk-scoped skill emit the same false gap.
  FIX: Check non-shadowed, non-disabled framework candidates against input.profile with scope "all". Ignore candidates excluded by "project-scope-mismatch". Treat the framework as covered when a non-disabled winning candidate passes under scope "all". Emit "incompatible-framework-policy" only when no active policy covers the framework and a non-disabled candidate fails language, architecture or principle checks. Otherwise emit "missing-framework-binding" when lookupFrameworkGuidance(framework) is undefined. Assert disabledResult.gaps is empty and add tests for scope-filtered, gwrk-scoped and mismatched implementation candidates in src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts. Run gates/phase-02.sh before the fix to observe RED.

Resolved review finding (code): Language matching and language gaps mishandle polyglot and custom language profiles — FR-001 and FR-002.
  WHERE: src/domain/policy-selection.ts:128-141,271-282,341
  EXPECTED: evaluateEnforcementCandidate matches both stack.language and stack.languages. Profiles with only stack.languages match each listed language, and mixed-workspace profiles retain stack.language alongside stack.languages. composeEffectivePolicy resolves languageGuidance from stack.language or stack.languages[0]. It checks every configured language and omits "missing-language-binding" when a compatible language skill covers that language.
  ACTUAL: Line 131 returns "language-mismatch" whenever stack.language is absent even when stack.languages lists Rust and Go. Line 135 ignores stack.language whenever stack.languages is non-empty, so TypeScript mismatches when stack.languages lists JavaScript and Python. Lines 272-282 ignore stack.languages and emit "missing-language-binding" for Kotlin even when a compatible Kotlin skill is selected.
  FIX: Collect normalized profile languages from both stack.language and stack.languages in evaluateEnforcementCandidate and composeEffectivePolicy. Resolve languageGuidance from stack.language or stack.languages[0]. Skip "unspecified" and "none". Emit "missing-language-binding" for a profile language only when lookupLanguageGuidance is undefined and no non-disabled winning candidate covers that language under scope "all". Add unit cases in src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts for languages-only profiles, mixed language overrides and custom Kotlin skills.

Resolved review finding (code): Architecture normalization diverges from resolveDesign and designRules — FR-002.
  WHERE: src/domain/policy-selection.ts:156-168,320-340
  EXPECTED: Policy selection normalizes architecture names with the same rules as resolveDesign in src/domain/architecture-context.ts lines 27-32. "Hexagonal-Functional", "hexagonal" and "hexagonal-with-functional-core" all resolve to "hexagonal-functional" across candidate matching, gap checks and architectureRules.
  ACTUAL: Lines 161 and 323 only call toLowerCase().trim(), while line 339 passes raw input.profile.design into designRules. A profile with architecture "Hexagonal-Functional" emits no "unbundled-architecture" gap while designRules falls through to the unbundled fallback rule. A profile or manifest using "hexagonal" fails candidate matching and reports "unbundled-architecture".
  FIX: Normalize architecture identifiers with trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, "-") and map "hexagonal" and "hexagonal-with-functional-core" to "hexagonal-functional". Use the normalized architecture in evaluateEnforcementCandidate, in the "unbundled-architecture" check and in the ProjectDesign passed to designRules. Add unit assertions in src/domain/policy-selection.test.ts for "hexagonal" and "Hexagonal-Functional" across profiles and manifests.

  WHERE: src/domain/policy-selection.ts:309-355

  ACTUAL: selectedSkills contains the built-in review skill. resolveCandidates(input, "all") lets the disabled implementation copy suppress it for coverage. gaps contains missing-language-binding and missing-framework-binding.
  FIX: Count the policies selected for the requested scope when computing coverage. Respect each workflow's own overrides when checking coverage across scopes. Add the same-name disabled implementation and active review copies to the phase gate.
